answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a deposit in a shared liquidity grove, where funds stay vested and cannot be withdrawn until a long cooling period ends. Any peer may then fund a willow branch of recomputation: if an identity output is proven false, that deposit is slashed and paid to the challenger. Sybils cannot timber the system with cheap fake nodes, because spawning ten thousand sock puppets means locking ten thousand real deposits — the attack cost scales linearly with the number of identities, which is exactly the defense.
